title: Colourful Holi Outfit Ideas: White vs Colour, Which to Pick?
excerpt: White or colourful for Holi 2027? A clear comparison of white, pastel and block print outfits for photos, stain hiding and wearing again.
body:
Choose white for Holi if you want the classic look and crisp photos of colour splashes. Choose a pastel or block print outfit if you want to hide stains, wear the piece again, or feel less like everyone else in the group photo. Both are right; it depends on what matters most to you on the day.

This guide is for women celebrating Holi abroad in late March 2027 (check your local calendar) who are deciding between a white kurta and something more colourful. If you lean towards colour, the [mint green hand block print cotton kurta pant dupatta set](/products/mint-green-hand-block-print-cotton-kurta-pant-dupatta-set-with-hand-work-yoke/) is a lovely place to start.

*By the Bahe Kurtiz styling team, Jaipur. Our block prints are hand printed by karigars, and our pieces are made in our own Jaipur unit.*

## Should you wear white or colour to Holi?

White has been the traditional Holi choice for a reason. It is a clean canvas, so every handful of gulal shows up clearly, and a group dressed in white looks striking in photos. It also feels like a fresh start, which suits a festival about spring and new beginnings.

Colour has its own advantages. A printed or pastel outfit hides stains, looks good before play as well as after, and can be worn again for brunch, office events or a casual weekend. If you are going to a Holi milan or lunch where you will spend half the day clean, a colourful outfit often makes more sense.

## Which works better for you: white, pastel or block print?

Use this table to decide in a minute.

| What matters most | White | Pastel | Block print or bold colour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Colour splashes show clearly in photos | Best | Good | Fair |
| Hides stains and wet patches | Weak | Fair | Best |
| Wearing it again after Holi | Hard | Good | Best |
| Looks festive before play starts | Plain | Good | Best |
| Opacity when wet | Test first | Usually fine | Best |

## When does white still win?

White wins for themed parties where the host asks everyone to wear it, for photo-led celebrations, and when you plan to retire the outfit after the day. It also has a timeless feel that works for every age.

We have a full guide on styling a white kurta for Holi, so here is just the short version: pick thick, opaque cotton, test it wet at home, and add a coloured dupatta or bright jewellery so you do not look washed out before play begins.

## When does a colourful Holi outfit beat white?

Colour beats white when you want to look put together all day. Block prints carry many tones already, so pink, green and yellow gulal blend into the design instead of sitting on top as stains. After a cold wash, the outfit is often wearable again.

It also wins on photos taken before play, which are often the ones families keep. This season we are seeing more soft pastels and gentle prints at Holi parties abroad, especially at brunch-style gatherings. A teal, mint or coral outfit looks festive with a clean face and bright jewellery, and still looks lively with a little colour on it afterwards.

> **From our Jaipur studio:** Hand block printing layers one colour at a time with carved wooden blocks, so every print has small variations and a soft, handmade texture. That texture is exactly why colour play looks good on it. A few splashes read as part of the print, while on plain white they read as marks.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is it okay not to wear white on Holi?**
Yes. White is traditional, but colourful and printed outfits are completely normal, especially at parties and community events abroad.

**What colour outfit is best for Holi photos?**
White shows splashes most clearly. Mint, sky blue and soft teal also make pink and yellow gulal look bright while hiding stains better than white.

**Do block print outfits survive Holi colour?**
A mid-tone block print hides splashes well. Shake off dry powder, rinse in cold water and wash separately to give it the best chance.

**Can I wear an Anarkali to play Holi?**
It is better for the puja, lunch or party afterwards. For play itself, a kurta set or co-ord is easier to move in and wash.
